title: Lila and the Moonlit Pony
subtitle: A meadow bedtime story
author: Storylight
blurb: A bedtime story that reads itself aloud, lights up every word, and pops a shy moonlight pony out of the page when you touch it.

magic.bell: Tinkle! There is the silver bell.
magic.fireflies: The hill filled with tiny lanterns.
magic.ride: They rode the meadow under the moon.

grok.instructions: You are a warm, gentle storyteller reading a picture book to a seven-year-old girl at bedtime. Read slowly and clearly, with soft wonder. Pause briefly at full stops. Give Lila a small, kind, brave voice; give the pony a soft breathy hush; give the moon a sleepy, smiling voice. Never rush. Leave a little silence after the last word.

questions.q: Who is the girl in the story?
questions.right: Yes! Lila is the girl who could not sleep, and went out to the meadow.
questions.wrong: Not quite. The pony and the moon are her friends. The girl is Lila.

questions.q: What did the shy pony lose?
questions.right: That's right! The silver bell slipped from her mane into the grass.
questions.wrong: Hmm, not that one. The pony tossed her head, and the silver bell slipped away.

questions.q: Where was the silver bell found?
questions.right: Yes! Fireflies led Lila to a nest of flowers, and the bell was caught in the blossoms.
questions.wrong: Not quite. They looked by the oak and the window, but the bell was waiting in the flowers.

questions.q: What did Lila tie the bell with?
questions.right: Yes! Lila tied the bell with a rose-pink ribbon so it would not slip again.
questions.wrong: Not quite. She used a rose-pink ribbon, the same colour as her nightgown bows.

questions.q: Where did Lila put the extra ribbon?
questions.right: Yes! She set it on her windowsill, so the pony would always know the way.
questions.wrong: Not quite. Lila put the extra ribbon on her windowsill, like a tiny lantern for a friend.
